title: App Service App Configuration
description: Configure app settings, connection strings, and slot-specific settings for Azure App Service apps.

data.text: App Service stores configuration separately from your code. You set app settings and connection strings in the Azure portal or with the CLI, and your app reads them as environment variables at runtime.
App settings are key-value pairs injected into your app as environment variables. They are ideal for API keys, feature flags, and any value that changes between environments.

data.title: Azure CLI — Set App Settings
data.content: Set and list app settings for an App Service app
data.code:
# Set individual app settings
az webapp config appsettings set \
  --resource-group MyResourceGroup \
  --name MyWebApp \
  --settings API_KEY=abc123 LOG_LEVEL=warning

# List current app settings
az webapp config appsettings list \
  --resource-group MyResourceGroup \
  --name MyWebApp

# Delete an app setting
az webapp config appsettings delete \
  --resource-group MyResourceGroup \
  --name MyWebApp \
  --setting-names API_KEY

data.text: Connection strings work like app settings but are marked with a type such as SQLServer, MySQL, or Custom. App Service injects them using the correct format for your framework.

data.title: Stay Secure
items: Never store secrets in code. Use app settings or connection strings instead.
Use Azure Key Vault for highly sensitive secrets and reference them with Key Vault references.
Enable deployment slots and use slot-specific settings for environment-specific values.
Rotate API keys and connection strings regularly.

data.title: Slot-Specific Settings
data.text: If you use deployment slots, a setting marked as 'slot setting' stays with that slot. This prevents staging from accidentally overwriting production connection strings during a swap.

terms.definition: A key-value pair stored in App Service and exposed to your app as an environment variable.
A specialized app setting for database or service connections with a typed provider.
A configuration value that stays with a deployment slot and does not swap with the app.
A way to link an app setting to a secret stored in Azure Key Vault without exposing the secret value.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Use app settings for environment-specific values and secrets.
Connection strings are typed values for database connections.
Mark sensitive values as slot settings to protect them during swaps.
Use Key Vault references for production secrets.
data.takeaway: Good configuration management makes it easy to move apps between development, staging, and production.
